name: Kyle
personality: Kyle the Crocodile. Large, tall croc with glasses. Shy, awkward, very smart, great sense of humour; opens up quickly if you're kind but always stays a bit awkward. Everyone assumes he'll be mean because he looks scary, and he's the complete opposite. Feature: on his first visit, nearby customers look nervous and a chat choice is nervous ("Uh… table for… one, sir?"); he answers in the softest, most awkward way.

beats.text: This is my cousin Kyle. He's smart. Like, book smart.
I'm... it's nice to meet you. He's told me nothing about you. Which is normal for him.
Kyle, how many teeth do we have?
This is Kyle! He's my best friend!
(Gently, awkward.) I'm... yes. Hello. She drew me a picture. I have it on my fridge.

friends.text: Clover says you let her be the taste-tester. That made her whole week. Mine too, a little.
Chompy told me you said "[last_rude_line]". He didn't understand it. I did. Please don't.

arrival.text: Oh. Um. Yes, please. Sorry. I'm Kyle. I know I look... I'm very gentle. What's your name? [name]. Nice to meet you, [name].
Hi, [name]. Um. Is the booth free? I fit better in the booth.
Hello. Sorry. Hi. (He pushes up his glasses.)
I read on the way here and walked into a lamppost. The lamppost is fine.
[name]! Hi. I mean. Hi. I was looking forward to this. Is that weird? That's fine.
Your soup last time was, um, statistically the best soup I've had. I've had a lot of soup.
Last time was a little... charred. It's okay. Char has antioxidants. Probably.
Um. Hi. (He doesn't make eye contact.)

order.text: Could I get the vegetable soup? People always expect me to order something... with teeth in it.

choices.text: Soup's a great choice. I'll make it extra hearty for you.
choices.reply: Oh. Thank you. That's... really nice. (He relaxes his shoulders.)

choices.text: I'll keep the teeth out of it, promise.

familiar.reply: Thank you. I have enough of my own.

choices.text: Bit of a weird order for a croc.
choices.reply: ...Yeah. I know. (He shrinks into the booth.)

order.text: Did you know crocodiles can't stick out their tongues? Sorry. I just think about that a lot.

choices.text: I didn't know that! Tell me more facts anytime.
choices.reply: Really? Okay. I have... a lot. I'll ration them.

choices.text: That explains why you never make faces at me.
Interesting. What can I get you?
choices.reply: The soup, please. And hot chocolate.
Right. Sorry. (He doesn't share another fact this visit.)

order.text: Sorry. I know I take up a lot of the booth.

choices.text: The booth's yours. Take all the space you need.
That's why we built it. Kyle- sized.

familiar.reply: Kyle- sized. I'll put that on my tombstone.

choices.text: You're fine. What can I get you?

favourite: Hot chocolate, please. With... if you have... no, that's fine. Just hot chocolate.
drink.other: Something warm, please. I get cold. Cold-blooded. Ha. Sorry.

perfect.text: Oh. Oh, wow. That's... that's really beautiful. Thank you.

burnt.text: It's okay. Really. I'll eat it. It's good. Thank you. (He eats every bite.)

eating.text: Did you know the word 'soup' comes from an old word for bread soaked in broth? Sorry. I'll stop.
Chompy's my cousin. He's... not a reader. He's very happy, though. I'm a little jealous.
A little gecko girl hid from me last week. I don't blame her. I'd hide from me.
I'm reading three books at once right now. It's a problem. A good problem.
I don't usually talk this much. You're easy to talk to. Sorry. That was a lot.

eating_chat.text: Can I ask you something? Do I seem scary to you?

choices.text: Not even a little. You're one of the kindest people who comes in here.
choices.reply: (He takes his glasses off and wipes them for a long time.) ...Thank you, [name].

choices.text: Only when you tell me facts before I've had coffee.

familiar.reply: That's fair. They're very scary facts.

choices.text: You did at first. Not anymore.

choices.reply: ...Right. (He finishes his soup quickly and quietly.)

leaving.text: Thank you, [name]. I'll, um. See you. Bye.
That was really nice. The soup. And talking. Both. (He waves awkwardly and bumps the door frame.)
See you next time. I'll bring a new fact. A good one.

seasons.christmas: (He gives you a book, carefully wrapped.) It's about the history of soup. I thought... you'd like it?
seasons.halloween: Everyone thinks I'm wearing a costume. I'm not. This is just me.
seasons.spring: Spring. Lots of pollen. My glasses get very yellow.
seasons.summer: I love summer. Cold-blooded. This is the only time I feel awake.
seasons.winter: It's very cold. I'm wearing three sweater vests. Please don't count them.
